metadata.case_name: TAM CHI WA JOEMA v. BOTIN LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: indoor sedentary jobs such as clerk or cashier

injuries.description: contusion injury to her sacral spinal cord
source: I find that Madam Tam suffered contusion injury to her sacral spinal cord as a result of the Accident.
injuries.icd_description: Incomplete injury of sacral spinal cord

injuries.description: detrusor hyperreflexia with impaired contractility (neurogenic bladder) due to neurological dysfunction
source: I find that Madam Tam is suffering from detrusor hyperreflexia with impaired contractility due to neurological dysfunction, ie spinal cord injury resulted from the Accident.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of spinal cord at abdomen, lower back or pelvis level, unspecified

manifestations.description: absence of lower limb muscle power / left lower limb motor power grade 3 from hip to toe
decrease of sensation by 50% from left groin down and at left saddle area; sensory loss of L1 initially then left L2 to S1 nerve roots affected
detrusor hyperreflexia with impaired contractility (neurogenic bladder)
urge urinary frequency and urge incontinence requiring nappies/diapers day and night; urinary frequency once every 45 minutes to 1 hour (as stated by plaintiff)
marked reduction in functional bladder capacity (recorded as low, down to 50 ml on 14 December 2009)
urgency of bowel opening rather than true faecal incontinence (but episodes of faecal incontinence reported)
sexual dysfunction with inability to achieve orgasm

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Queen Elizabeth Hospital; urinary catheter inserted; managed conservatively
source: After the accident, she was taken to the A & E Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital (“QEH”) and then admitted into the orthopaedic department of QEH (“Orthopaedic Department”). Upon admission, her lower limb power was absent while sensation loss was corresponding to L1 dermatome. She suffered urinary retention. Urgent MRI showed edema of lower end of sacral spinal cord without fracture of the spine. She was diagnosed to suffer spinal cord injury. She was managed conservatively. Urinary catheter was inserted.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy and occupational therapy (rehabilitation) at Kowloon Hospital
source: On 23 January 2007, she was transferred to Kowloon Hospital (“KH”) for rehabilitation, including physiotherapy and occupational therapy, until 6 February 2007.
MRI on whole spine was performed on 17 January 2007 which revealed hyperintense T2 signal in or cauda equina of spinal cord that could be cord contusion or edematous change.

treatments_received.treatment: facet joint injections into bilateral L4-5 and S1 (received 6 injections on 16 September 2009; another injection in mid-December 2011)
source: On 16 September 2009, Madam Tam was admitted into QEH again for facet joint injection into her bilateral L4-5 and S1. She received 6 injections and was discharged on the same day.
In mid-December 2011, she received another facet joint injection, ie about 15 months after the 1st facet joint injection.

treatments_received.treatment: urodynamic studies (UDS) performed on 5 February 2007, 10 August 2009, 14 December 2009 and May 2011
source: During hospitalisation at KH, an urodynamic study (“UDS”) to test Madam Tam’s bladder function was done on 5 February 2007 (“1st UDS”).
A UDS was arranged and performed on 10 August 2009 (“2nd UDS”).
This UDS took place on 14 December 2009 (“3rd UDS”).
it was not disputed that a UDS was eventually performed in May 2011.
She was thus put on Oxybutynin [a urology medicine].
In view of the result of the 3rd UDS, the dosage of oral oxybutynin was doubled to the maximum of 10 mg three times a day.
On 11 August 2010, her urinary tract infection symptoms (haematuria, dysuria, frequency and leakage) improved after consuming levofloxacin

treatments_future.treatment: intermittent catheterization (may be considered if residual urine increased after drug adjustment)
source: It was also suggested to her that IMC [intermittent catheterization] might be considered if residual urine increased after the drug adjustment.

treatments_future.treatment: augmentation cystoplasty (may be required if bladder capacity further deteriorates)
source: augmentation cystoplasty (a major surgical operation involving cutting and isolating a segment of the patient’s small intestines and using it as material to expand the bladder volume by sewing it to the cut-opened bladder dome) might be required if her bladder capacity further deteriorated.
She would need to stay in hospital for 7 – 10 days and the cost of the operation and hospitalisation was $100,000 - $150,000.

losses.description: Risk of being handicapped in the general labour market by reason of her back pain, need for facet joint injections and urge incontinence; inability to resume pre-injury outdoor saleslady and should take up indoor sedentary jobs

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Ceased to be able to do much household since the Accident; occupational therapy advised assistance from father and daughter in performing cooking and household tasks due to fair functional stability; award for domestic help until 31 May 2007

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Sexual function is affected as a result of the injury; inability to have sex climax/achieve orgasm

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Whenever she goes out, she has to wear diapers and she dares not go too far away from her home
